body: claimed: issue-worker-high (claude-opus-5-5) · 2026-11-15T13:07Z · worktree/branch issue/1842-g76-schedule-sources · plan: settle the four G76 readings from published sources; pin or fix; record in docs/decisions/1842.

fix on issue/1842-g76-schedule-sources · PR #1897 · pinned by each_pass_starts_on_the_crest_flank_line_along_the_travel, every_pass_runs_to_the_posted_end_z_inside_the_root_pass, the_minimum_depth_clamps_the_cut_of_one_pass · merges when reviewed

Findings for the four readings. No Fanuc control or simulator was used.

Sources:
- S1: FANUC Series 0i-MODEL F Operator's Manual, Lathe System, B-64604EN-1/01, section 4.2.7 "Multiple Threading Cycle (G76)", pages 82-85, Fig. 4.2.7 (a) and (b). https://www.drivesul.com.br/template/imagens/manuais/manuais-fanuc/fanuc-series-0i-model-f/FANUC%20Series%200i%20MODEL%20F%20-%20OPERATOR_S%20MANUAL%20-%20Lathe%20System.pdf
- S2: Siemens SINUMERIK ISO Turning Programming Manual 07/2022, A5E52211627B AA, section 4.1 "Multiple-thread cutting cycle (G76)", pages 87-89, Fig. 4-25 and 4-26. https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/914/109813914/att_1116680/v1/ONE_iso_turning_progr_man_0722_en-US.pdf

1. Z shift: **settled, the post is correct.** In S1 and S2 the start point A is above the crest point B, at the same Z. Each pass starts on the line from B at a/2. Deeper passes start further along the direction of travel. Both sources say that one edge cuts.
2. End Z: **settled, the post is correct.** S1: "Coordinates of the cutting end point (point D ...)". S2: "Endpoint of thread in the direction of Z axis". In both figures, every pass ends at D. The kernel lays the shallower passes short of D. The control cuts them to D, inside the groove of the root pass. This is not a gouge risk. #1896 (P7) tracks it.
3. Minimum depth: **settled, the post is correct.** S1: "When the cutting depth of one cycle operation becomes smaller than this limit, the cutting depth is clamped at this value." S2 writes the same clamp on "(Δd - Δd-1)". The clamp is on the cut of one pass below the pass before it.
4. Rounding: **open.** S1 and S2 confirm the units: dmin, Δd and k in the least increment without a decimal point, R(d) with a decimal point. No source states how the control rounds Δd·√n. The post's guard stays. Only a run on a control can settle this.

The open question (refuse flank G76) is answered: no refusal is necessary, because readings 1 and 2 are settled. The PR uses `Refs #1842`. This issue stays open for reading 4.

Public documentation search results for the four unconfirmed G76 items in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`.

Two-block Fanuc G76 word order: block 1 uses `G76` with six-digit `P(m)(r)(a)` (finish pass count `m`, chamfer pull-out `r`, tool angle `a`), minimum depth `Q`, and finish allowance `R`. Block 2 uses `G76` with target diameter `X`, target length `Z`, optional taper `R`, thread height `P`, first depth `Q`, and lead `F`.

| Point | Finding | Source | Confidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1. Z-shift sign and programmed Z pass | Fanuc, Siemens ISO, Mitsubishi, GSK, and Centroid manuals describe single-edge flank cutting for non-zero tool angle `a`. Allowed tool angles are 0, 29, 30, 55, 60, and 80 on Fanuc and GSK, or 00 to 99 on Mitsubishi. These manuals do not state which pass sits at programmed start Z, or give the Z-shift formula. LinuxCNC single-block G76 shifts earlier passes back so deeper passes move in the Z cut direction, and its root pass sits at programmed start Z. This does not match `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, which shifts start Z to `c_first - k*tan(a/2)` and puts depth zero at programmed start Z. | Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D ISO Turning Manual (Entry ID 109769430, https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/document/109769430/sinumerik-840d-sl-iso-turning?dti=0&lc=en-WW); Fanuc Parameter Manuals (`drivesul.com.br`, Param 5143); Mitsubishi M70/M80/M700 Programming Manual (`mitsubishielectric.com`); GSK980TD and GSK988TA Manuals (`gskcnc.com`: "thread run-in path of roughing is from its top to bottom"); LinuxCNC docs (`linuxcnc.org`) and RS274NGC source `convert_threading_cycle` (https://github.com/LinuxCNC/linuxcnc/blob/master/src/emc/rs274ngc/interp_convert.cc) | not found |
| 2. End-Z shift | Fanuc, Siemens ISO, Mitsubishi, Centroid, and Haas manuals define `Z` in block 2 as the thread end point and maximum thread length. These manuals do not state a depth-based shift past programmed end Z. Only chamfer pull-out `r` changes end motion inside the thread length. Fanuc-compatible manuals do not state whether every intermediate roughing pass stops at exact end Z or pulls out early. In LinuxCNC, earlier roughing passes shift back before end Z, and only the root pass reaches end Z. | Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D ISO Turning Manual (Entry ID 109769430, https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/document/109769430/sinumerik-840d-sl-iso-turning?dti=0&lc=en-WW); Fanuc Manuals (`drivesul.com.br`: "cutting end point (Point D)"); Haas Lathe Operator Manual (`haascnc.com`: "Z-axis absolute location, maximum thread length"); Centroid CNC12 Lathe Operator Manual Ch. 11 and 12 (https://www.centroidcnc.com/centroid_diy/downloads/operator_manuals/centroid-cnc12-lathe-operator-manual.pdf); LinuxCNC RS274NGC source `convert_threading_cycle` (https://github.com/LinuxCNC/linuxcnc/blob/master/src/emc/rs274ngc/interp_convert.cc) | not found |
| 3. Minimum-depth clamp | Siemens ISO and Mitsubishi manuals confirm the `Q(dmin)` clamp rule. When the calculated step becomes smaller than `Q(dmin)`, the control clamps the pass depth to `Q(dmin)` for later roughing passes until finish allowance `R`. Because square-root pass steps decrease with each pass, clamping from the previous clamped depth gives the same schedule as `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`. Manuals do not state how the control splits a final roughing cut smaller than `Q(dmin)` before finish depth `k - d`. | Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D ISO Turning Manual (Entry ID 109769430, https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/document/109769430/sinumerik-840d-sl-iso-turning?dti=0&lc=en-WW: "the cutting depth remains bound to the value specified with the address Q"); Mitsubishi M70/M80/M700 Programming Manual (`mitsubishielectric.com`: "If the calculated cut amount is smaller than Δdmin, it is clamped by Δdmin."); Centroid CNC12 Lathe Operator Manual Ch. 12 Param 51 (https://www.centroidcnc.com/centroid_diy/downloads/operator_manuals/centroid-cnc12-lathe-operator-manual.pdf: "this parameter sets the minimum depth increment"); CNCzone and IndustryArena user threads (`cnczone.com`, `industryarena.com`) | stated in the source |
| 4. Rounding | Manuals state that block-1 `Q(dmin)` and block-2 `P(k)` and `Q(first depth)` use whole least increments without a decimal point. One least increment is 0.001 mm or 0.0001 inch in IS-B, and 0.0001 mm or 0.00001 inch in IS-C. Modern Fanuc, Siemens ISO, Mitsubishi, and GSK988TA controls accept a decimal value for finish allowance `R(d)`. Early Fanuc 0-T software had different integer-or-decimal rules for `R(d)`. Manuals do not state how the control rounds internal square-root pass depths, or state a one-increment rule for `R`. | Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D ISO Turning Manual (Entry ID 109769430, https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/document/109769430/sinumerik-840d-sl-iso-turning?dti=0&lc=en-WW); Fanuc Parameter Manuals (`drivesul.com.br`, Param 5140 and 5141); GSK988TA Manual (`gskcnc.com`, Param 5141); CNCzone and IndustryArena user threads (`cnczone.com`, `industryarena.com`) | not found |

## Not found

- **Programmed start Z pass for Fanuc when tool angle `a` is not 0**: Public Fanuc, Siemens ISO, Mitsubishi, GSK, and Centroid manuals do not state whether programmed start Z puts the depth-zero crest at `G00 Z` (as `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` assumes) or puts the root pass at `G00 Z` (as LinuxCNC `interp_convert.cc` does).
- **Z-shift formula on Fanuc two-block G76**: Public Fanuc-compatible manuals do not state the pass offset equation for flank infeed. LinuxCNC `interp_convert.cc` moves deeper passes in the Z cut direction, but LinuxCNC uses a different single-block G76 format.
- **Intermediate pass end Z on Fanuc when tool angle `a` is not 0**: Manuals define block-2 `Z` as the thread end point and maximum thread length, so no overshoot past `Z` is documented. Manuals do not state whether earlier roughing passes end at exact `Z` or stop early like LinuxCNC.
- **Final roughing step below `Q(dmin)`**: Manuals do not state how the control handles a final roughing cut smaller than `Q(dmin)` right before finish depth `k - d`, or when first depth is smaller than `Q(dmin)`.
- **Internal rounding and one-increment `R` rule**: Manuals do not state how the control rounds internal square-root depths between passes, or state a one-increment tolerance on `R`.

## Suggested changes for `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`

These are suggestions only (no code changes made):

1. **Warn or refuse when tool angle `a` is not 0**: For the open question in this issue, make `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` warn or refuse non-zero `InfeedAngle` until hardware tests check items 1 and 2, because LinuxCNC anchors the root pass at programmed Z instead of depth zero.
2. **Add an option for integer `R` finish allowance**: Block 1 in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `R` as a decimal (`fu`), which matches Fanuc 0i, Siemens ISO, Mitsubishi, and GSK988TA. Add a post option to write `R` in whole least increments (`um`) for early Fanuc 0-T controls.
3. **Add a least-increment scale option for IS-C controls**: `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` uses fixed IS-B scaling (`0.001 mm` or `0.0001 inch`) for integer `P` and `Q` words. Add an IS-B or IS-C option (or document IS-B clearly in the post) because IS-C integer words are ten times larger.
4. **Document tool angle pairing clearly**: Keep the allowed check for 0, 29, 30, 55, 60, and 80 in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` for Fanuc and GSK controls, and document that `InfeedAngle` is twice `flank_angle` so users select half of the target tool angle (`14.5`, `27.5`, or `30`). Keep Mitsubishi (`00` to `99`) and Haas (`P1` to `P4`, single-block `K` and `D`) separate if added later.

## Real-control check

A check on a real Fanuc control is still necessary before you cut metal. Test non-zero tool angles, final roughing step behavior, and finish allowance `R` format in air or scrap before production cutting.

PR #1897 is merged (f43343076). It added tests only and it does not close this issue. The controller run for the Fanuc G76 Z-shift sign and the end-Z reading is still open. The label `in-review` is removed because no PR is open.
